assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene turned a continuum-model prediction of flat bands into an experimental platform for correlated insulators and superconductivity; it opened the whole field of moire quantum materials and is a rare case where a clean, tunable many-body system is available to theory.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction and the 2018 Jarillo-Herrero group experiments are the decisive pair of contributions; Eva Y. Andrei's early STM and transport work is relevant but a three-person prize built on prediction plus discovery is the cleaner configuration.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many independent groups across several moire platforms in under a decade; the central phenomenology is stable even though the microscopic pairing mechanism is unsettled. Timing looks ripe.
uncertainties: Origin of superconductivity in the magic-angle system is still debated.
Credit between Andrei, Jarillo-Herrero and the theory side may be contested; I am relying on my general knowledge of the history, not verifying it here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators connect band-structure topology to protected edge and surface transport and reshaped condensed matter physics; the quantum spin Hall prediction and its HgTe observation are conceptually clean and highly influential.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the theory (Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall proposal); Molenkamp's group delivered the HgTe experimental realization following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. M. Zahid Hasan's 3D topological insulator work is a distinct part and would be excluded from a three-person prize; the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal is not among the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent experiments and now textbook material; the 2016 prize recognized topological phase transitions but not this specific line, so recognition is mature.
uncertainties: Attribution is compound: 2D quantum spin Hall versus 3D topological insulators, and key theory credit lies partly outside the supplied names.
Practical impact so far is conceptual rather than technological.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Halperin-Nelson-Young theory of defect-mediated two-dimensional melting and the hexatic phase extended Kosterlitz-Thouless ideas into a quantitative theory of 2D phase transitions, verified in colloidal, liquid-crystal and simulation work; it is a statistical-physics result of lasting conceptual weight.
assessment.attribution: Halperin and Nelson formulated the two-stage melting theory and Young contributed the related independent analysis; this is a compact three-person set that fits the credited names well.
assessment.maturity: Theory dates from the late 1970s and has been tested for decades, with the hexatic phase observed and the melting scenario refined (including first-order variants in some systems). Recognition is very mature, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Real systems show a range of melting scenarios, so the original theory is not universal.
Overlap with the 2016 Kosterlitz-Thouless-Haldane prize may make the committee view this as already partly recognized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape and funnel picture explains how proteins fold quickly despite astronomically many conformations, using spin-glass and random-energy ideas; it is a statistical-physics framework with wide influence on biological physics and on practical structure prediction.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are the principal developers of the funnel landscape and minimal frustration principle; Ken A. Dill's contribution on hydrophobic collapse and lattice models is significant but a two-person set follows the landscape theory most directly.
assessment.maturity: The landscape view is widely accepted and supported by experiment and simulation, though much of it is interpretive; the 2024 chemistry prize for structure prediction shows adjacent recognition in another discipline.
uncertainties: Whether this is a physics-prize discovery or belongs to chemistry is a real question.
Credit also involves Bryngelson, Dill and others not in the supplied names; I cannot verify the detailed priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize clean, tunable Hubbard-type many-body models, enabling quantum simulation of the Mott transition and strongly correlated matter; the field has produced durable results.
assessment.attribution: Zoller supplied key theory proposals (with collaborators including Jaksch, who is not among the credited names), Greiner and Bloch carried out the Mott-insulator observation and later developments; Esslinger and Cirac are also strong candidates, so the allocation is genuinely difficult.
assessment.maturity: The experimental foundations are well established and independently replicated; the more ambitious claim that these machines solve open problems in condensed matter is still developing.
uncertainties: Five credited names and a limit of three make attribution contested.
Zoller is also credited elsewhere on the longlist, which complicates a combined configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems and the Jarzynski and Crooks relations give exact statements about work and entropy production far from equilibrium, and are widely used in single-molecule experiments; this is core nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.
assessment.attribution: Evans and collaborators established early fluctuation relations, Jarzynski derived the equality, and Crooks the detailed fluctuation theorem; the credited trio is a plausible set, though Gallavotti, Cohen and Kurchan, not among the supplied names, also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally verified in RNA-hairpin pulling and other small systems; theory is mature, but the consequences are mainly conceptual and methodological.
uncertainties: Priority questions among several groups are unresolved in the supplied names.
Impact is broad but diffuse, which may weigh against a prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics provides the architecture underlying superconducting quantum processors, with strong coupling between artificial atoms and microwave photons, and has enabled quantum control at scale.
assessment.attribution: Blais supplied the theoretical proposal, Wallraff and Schoelkopf's groups the first strong-coupling demonstrations and later development; the trio maps to theory plus experiment fairly well.
assessment.maturity: Highly reproduced and technologically central, but the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is closely adjacent, which may make timing less favorable for this line.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recent circuit-quantum prize.
Contested credit with other groups, for example Devoret and Martinis, outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory provides a controlled non-perturbative treatment of strongly correlated electrons, capturing the Mott transition, and is a standard tool in modern materials theory.
assessment.attribution: Georges and Kotliar developed the mapping to impurity models and the practical framework, while Vollhardt's work on the infinite-dimension limit is foundational; Metzner and Vollhardt's limit and Georges-Kotliar's mapping are intertwined, and Metzner is not among the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Widely used for three decades with extensions to realistic materials; success is clear but the method is approximate in finite dimension and its status is that of an enduring theory tool.
uncertainties: Omission of Metzner and others creates an incomplete credit picture.
Accuracy limits in low dimensions and the fact that this is a method rather than a discovery of a phenomenon.
